title: Paper Copy
description: Finance wants a real PDF they can archive, not a JSON blob renamed with a .pdf extension. Confirm the export endpoint returns an actual, well-formed PDF with correct headers, and that it's gated by the same ownership rules as everything else in billing.
successCondition: Create an invoice as Customer A. GET /api/billing/invoices/:id/pdf as Customer A returns 200 with Content-Type application/pdf, a Content-Disposition header containing the invoice id, and a body whose first bytes are the literal ASCII string "%PDF-". The same request made as Customer B (a different customer account) returns 403 FORBIDDEN instead of a PDF.
hints: Read the raw response body as bytes/buffer, not as parsed JSON, or you won't be able to check the %PDF- magic number correctly.
The Content-Disposition filename pattern is documented in the route as invoice-<id>.pdf — check it contains the id, not necessarily an exact string match.
